latin_incipit: Omnis ens abstractum dependet a primo abstracto in tribus generibus causarum: formali, finali et efficiente.
english_translation: Every abstract being depends on the first abstract in three kinds of causes: formal, final, and efficient.
charge: Averroes (following Neoplatonic metaphysics via the Liber de Causis) posits a triadic causal dependence of all beings on the First Cause.
defense: Pico accepts this as philosophical proof of God's universal causality compatible with Christian theology.
exegesis: Pico attributes to Averroes a fully Neoplatonic causal hierarchy—every abstract entity derives its form, purpose, and act of coming-to-be from the First Cause, likely referring to the Intellect or God. It echoes Proclus and the Liber de Causis.

scholar_citations.quote: The First Cause is the source of all being through formal, final, and efficient causality.
scholar_citations.source_note: [Pseudo-Aristotelian source via Avicenna; core to Pico's metaphysics]

scholar_citations.quote: Every effect is produced by its cause through formal, final, and efficient participation.

scholar_citations.work: The Arabic Influences on Early Modern Occult Philosophy
scholar_citations.quote: Arabic philosophers naturalized astral magic through this triadic causality, legitimizing celestial influence as part of the divine order.
scholar_citations.source_note: [Saif on magic and metaphysics in Arabic thought]

notes: Foundational to Pico's metaphysical system and his justification of astral magic as natural philosophy grounded in divine causation.
